about: Stella's owner-facing alert codes (D44). bin/alert.sh renders #alerts messages from this file; bin/alert-catalog.sh --docs writes docs/alert-codes.md from it. A code is never reused or renumbered: retire one with "status": "retired". Placeholders: {name}, filled from the caller's key=value pairs; {since} and {now} are times, shown in the owner's time zone; {what} is the plain phrase for the caller's error=.

alerts.title: self-check is failing
alerts.message: The automatic {check} failed on the latest version of the stack (commit {commit}).{detail} Stella keeps running, but one of her own checks no longer passes.
alerts.action: ask Claude Code to run the tests. Nothing else is needed from you right now.
alerts.cause: A recent change broke a test, the code style check (lint) or the build; or a test depends on something outside the container that changed. A test that fails once is run again on its own first, so only a test that fails twice in a row raises this alert.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/watchdog.log (full test output, and a line `flaky:` for a test that failed once and passed on the rerun); .supervisor/status.json (which step, exit code); `npm test` in the container.
alerts.resolved_message: The automatic checks pass again on commit {commit}. They were failing from {since} to {now}.

alerts.title: self-check got stuck
alerts.message: The automatic {check} did not finish in time and was stopped (commit {commit}). Stella keeps running, but her own checks cannot complete.
alerts.action: ask Claude Code to run the tests and find the one that hangs.
alerts.cause: A test waits forever (a network call, a lock, a prompt for input), or the container is badly overloaded. The step is killed after WATCHDOG_STEP_TIMEOUT (600 s).
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/watchdog.log (output up to the kill); .supervisor/status.json ("hung": true).
alerts.resolved_message: The automatic checks finish and pass again on commit {commit}. They were stuck from {since} to {now}.

alerts.title: Stella's program is not running
alerts.message: No running program for Stella's Discord connection was found, and she was not paused on purpose. She cannot see or answer messages until it runs again.
alerts.action: run the Windows recovery script, or ask Claude Code to restart Stella (see STL-GW-101 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The gateway process crashed or was stopped, or the container restarted without starting it. The check is a process lookup, so it says nothing about the Discord connection itself.
alerts.check: docs/recovery.md; `tmux ls` and `hermes status` in the container; ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log.
alerts.resolved_message: Stella's Discord program is running again. It was reported as not running from {since} to {now}; at {now} the check saw: {parts}.

parts.quiet: her program is running and the newest connection line in her log says connected; nothing was written for a while, which is normal when nobody writes to her
parts.settings: the settings for this check are missing or invalid
parts.process_check: the check could not look for her program
parts.logs: her log files cannot be read
parts.no_marker: her program is running, but her log shows no connection line and nothing new for an hour
parts.check: the check itself did not run
parts._other: something the check could not name

alerts.title: Stella lost her Discord connection
alerts.message: Stella's log shows her Discord connection dropped at {at} and has not come back since. Her program is still running and keeps retrying, but she may not see or answer messages until it connects.
alerts.action: wait a few minutes: she usually reconnects by herself, and a ✅ message follows. If it does not, send her a message in Discord, and if she does not answer ask Claude Code to restart her (see STL-GW-102 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: Discord or the container's network dropped the connection and the reconnect attempts keep failing (DNS, network, a Discord outage, revoked access). The check reads the newest connection line in her log; it is not a live test, and a quiet log alone never raises this.
alerts.check: ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log (the last `[Discord] Disconnected` / `Reconnect` lines); `bin/watchdog_settings.py gateway` (the verdict and its evidence); `hermes status`; docs/recovery.md.
alerts.resolved_message: Stella's Discord connection looks healthy again. The loss was reported from {since} to {now}; at {now} the check saw: {parts}.

parts.quiet: her program is running and the newest connection line in her log says connected; nothing was written for a while, which is normal when nobody writes to her
parts.settings: the settings for this check are missing or invalid
parts.process_check: the check could not look for her program
parts.logs: her log files cannot be read
parts.no_marker: her program is running, but her log shows no connection line and nothing new for an hour
parts.check: the check itself did not run
parts._other: something the check could not name

alerts.title: can't tell if Stella is connected
alerts.message: The automatic check could not find out whether Stella's Discord connection works: {parts}. This alone does not prove that Stella is down.
alerts.action: ask Claude Code to look at the watchdog (see STL-GW-103 in docs/alert-codes.md). Nothing else is needed from you right now.
alerts.cause: The watchdog settings file is missing or invalid, the process lookup could not run, the log files cannot be read, or Stella's program runs but her log shows no connection line and nothing new for an hour.
alerts.check: `bin/watchdog_settings.py --check`; `bin/watchdog_settings.py gateway` (the verdict and its evidence); .supervisor/logs/watchdog.log.
alerts.resolved_message: The check can tell again whether Stella is connected. It could not tell from {since} to {now}; at {now} it saw: {parts}.

parts.quiet: her program is running and the newest connection line in her log says connected; nothing was written for a while, which is normal when nobody writes to her
parts.settings: the settings for this check are missing or invalid
parts.process_check: the check could not look for her program
parts.logs: her log files cannot be read
parts.no_marker: her program is running, but her log shows no connection line and nothing new for an hour
parts.check: the check itself did not run
parts._other: something the check could not name
parts.state_stale: her program is running and her log says connected, but she stopped updating her own status, so she may be stuck

alerts.title: not watching for your replies
alerts.message: The part of Stella that reads your replies in escalation threads has not run for {minutes} minutes. Your replies are not picked up, and finished cards are not reported, until it runs again.
alerts.action: it usually starts again by itself. If it is still here after 15 minutes, ask Claude Code to check the reply checker (see STL-ESC-201 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The container's scheduled jobs (cron) stopped, the container restarted, or bin/escalation-reply-poll.sh is stuck or failing at start.
alerts.check: .supervisor/state/reply-poll.heartbeat (time of the last run); `crontab -l`; run bin/escalation-reply-poll.sh by hand and read its output.
alerts.resolved_message: The part of Stella that reads your replies runs again. The check saw no run from {since} to {now}.

alerts.title: can't read replies in an escalation thread
alerts.message: Stella tried {count} times in a row and could not read the thread for card {card} ({what}). Replies there are not being seen until this clears.
alerts.action: it usually clears when the connection recovers. If it is still here after an hour, see STL-ESC-210 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Network or DNS trouble, a dropped secure connection, a Discord outage or rate limit, the thread was deleted by hand, or the bot lost access to #escalations. A short Discord or network drop (a minute or two) is the usual case: the alert needs only 3 failed reads in a row, and Stella keeps reading every few seconds.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log and .supervisor/escalations.log (POLL_FAIL lines hold the raw error and the thread id); `bin/owner-config.sh --verify`.
alerts.resolved_title: replies in an escalation thread are read again
alerts.resolved_message: Stella can read the thread for card {card} again. It could not from {since} to {now}; replies posted meanwhile are picked up now.

alerts.title: can't read the task board
alerts.message: Stella could not read her task board, so your replies and finished cards are not being processed until it works again.
alerts.action: nothing yet, Stella will retry every minute. If it is still here after an hour, ask Claude Code to check the board (see STL-ESC-211 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The kanban database is locked or damaged, the ~/.hermes volume is full or unreadable, or the hermes command is missing from the job's PATH.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (POLL_FAIL "kanban list failed"); `hermes kanban list` in the container.

alerts.title: couldn't pass your reply on to its card
alerts.message: Your reply for card {card} was seen, but Stella could not pass it on to the card. She tries again every minute.
alerts.action: nothing, Stella will retry. If it is still here after an hour, see STL-ESC-212 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The kanban unblock call failed: the card changed state meanwhile, the board is locked, or the hermes command failed.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (UNBLOCK_FAIL for the card); `hermes kanban show <card>`.

alerts.title: an escalation was not posted
alerts.message: Card {card} ("{title}") needs a decision from you, but Stella could not post it in #escalations ({what}). The card stays blocked.
alerts.action: nothing yet, Stella tries again up to 3 times over the next 20 minutes. The question is also on the card itself.
alerts.cause: Discord was unreachable or refused the request, the #escalations channel id in the owner settings is wrong, or another run held the card's lock.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log and .supervisor/escalations.log (THREAD_FAIL with the raw error); `bin/owner-config.sh --verify`.

alerts.title: an escalation could not be posted after 3 tries
alerts.message: Card {card} ("{title}") needs a decision from you, but Stella could not post it in #escalations after 3 tries. She has stopped trying, and the card stays blocked.
alerts.action: ask Claude Code to look at card {card} and post its escalation again (see STL-ESC-221 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The same causes as STL-ESC-220, lasting over 20 minutes.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (THREAD_FAIL and THREAD_RETRY for the card); .supervisor/state/thread-retry.tsv; `bin/escalation-thread.sh --check`.

alerts.title: escalation notice missing in #supervisor
alerts.message: The question for card {card} was posted in its escalation thread, but the notice in #supervisor could not be posted ({what}). You will not see it there.
alerts.action: open #escalations, find the thread for card {card}, and reply there as usual.
alerts.cause: The #supervisor channel id in the owner settings is wrong, the bot lost access to #supervisor, or Discord was unreachable.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (LINK_FAIL with the raw error); `bin/owner-config.sh --verify`.

alerts.title: a card is stuck in a loop
alerts.message: Card {card} ("{title}") was blocked again after you already answered twice ({count} blocks so far). Stella has stopped asking you and holds it for a closer look.
alerts.action: ask Claude Code to look at card {card}; your replies no longer unblock it on their own.
alerts.cause: The worker does not act on the answer (a misread reply, a missing ability, or the card asks for something impossible).
alerts.check: the card's comments (`hermes kanban show <card>`); .supervisor/escalations.log (LOOP_HELD).

alerts.title: a card's builder can't do it
alerts.message: Card {card} ("{title}") stopped because its builder hit something it cannot do (a missing tool, access or skill). This is not a question for you, so no escalation thread was opened.
alerts.action: read the comment on card {card}, then give it to another builder (the Claude builder can do more) or change the card.
alerts.cause: The builder's tools or model cannot do the task; the exact error is in the card comment.
alerts.check: the card's comment "Capability block held for triage" (`hermes kanban show <card>`); .supervisor/escalations.log (CAPABILITY_HELD).

alerts.title: ignored a reply from someone else
alerts.message: Someone who is not the configured owner replied in the escalation thread for card {card}. The reply was not applied. If that was you, your Discord user id in the owner settings is wrong.
alerts.action: if it was you, correct your Discord user id in the owner settings; STL-ESC-240 in docs/alert-codes.md says how. The reply is then applied within a minute.
alerts.cause: OWNER_DISCORD_USER_ID in config/owner.env is not your id, or another member of the server replied.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (REPLY_IGNORED_NOT_OWNER with the author id); to fix: `chmod u+w config config/owner.env`, edit it, then `chmod 555 config; chmod 444 config/owner.env` (from Windows, just edit it).

alerts.title: owner settings are missing or unreadable
alerts.message: Stella cannot read the owner settings, so escalations are stopped: no new threads are opened and replies are not applied.{fix}
alerts.action: correct the owner settings (the example file shows every accepted form) or recreate them from it; STL-CFG-301 in docs/alert-codes.md says how.
alerts.cause: config/owner.env is missing (a fresh clone or a deleted file), unreadable, has a malformed line, or lacks a required key.
alerts.check: `bin/owner-config.sh --check` (names the problem); .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (raw error); copy config/owner.example.env to config/owner.env and fill it in (docs/recovery.md).

alerts.title: your Discord user id in the settings is not valid
alerts.message: The owner's Discord user id in the settings is empty or not a valid Discord id, so Stella ignores every reply and reaction in the escalation threads until it is fixed. Replies already posted are applied after the fix.
alerts.action: correct your Discord user id in the owner settings; STL-CFG-302 in docs/alert-codes.md says how.
alerts.cause: OWNER_DISCORD_USER_ID in config/owner.env is empty or not 17 to 20 digits (a typo, a username instead of the id, extra characters).
alerts.check: `bin/owner-config.sh --check`; to fix: `chmod u+w config config/owner.env`, edit it, then `chmod 555 config; chmod 444 config/owner.env` (from Windows, just edit it).

alerts.title: a Claude request was held (limit reached)
alerts.message: A request to Claude {model} for card {card} was not sent because one of Stella's usage limits is reached. It is saved and can be sent later.
alerts.action: nothing right now. When the limit resets, ask Claude Code to send the held requests (see STL-LIM-401 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: All Opus slots are busy (OPUS_MAX_CONCURRENT), or the Haiku daily limit (HAIKU_MAX_PER_DAY) is used up, or a limit is set to 0.
alerts.check: .supervisor/limits.env; `bin/escalate-drain.sh --list`; .supervisor/escalations.log (QUEUED, LIMIT).

alerts.title: Claude usage is used up
alerts.message: Claude has no usage left right now, so a {model} request for card {card} was not sent. It is saved and can be sent later.
alerts.action: nothing until the usage resets. Then ask Claude Code to send the held requests (see STL-LIM-402 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The Claude subscription's session or weekly limit, or the organisation's usage credits, are used up.
alerts.check: `bin/escalate-drain.sh --list`; .supervisor/escalations.log (POOL_EXHAUSTED with the matched message).

alerts.title: a Claude request was answered by a fallback model
alerts.message: Claude has no usage left right now, so a {model} request for card {card} was answered by a different, free model ({served}) through the OmniRoute gateway. The answer is labelled as a fallback; it is not a Claude answer.
alerts.action: nothing, unless the card is important: check the fallback answer before relying on it, and send the request to Claude later if it matters (see STL-LIM-404 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The Claude subscription's limit was reached (STL-LIM-402) on a low-risk card and the fallback is switched on (`enabled: true` in docs/hermes-local/fallback-routing.json). High-risk cards are never rerouted.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (POOL_EXHAUSTED then FALLBACK, with the serving model); the card's comments; the OmniRoute gateway on loopback.

alerts.title: the list of held Claude requests is full
alerts.message: Stella already holds {max} Claude requests that could not be sent. New ones are refused and not saved until the list is cleared.
alerts.action: ask Claude Code to look at the held requests and send or clear them (see STL-LIM-403 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: Limits or an exhausted usage pool held many requests and nobody sent them (QUEUE_MAX, default 50).
alerts.check: `bin/escalate-drain.sh --list`; .supervisor/state/queue.jsonl.

alerts.title: Stella's settings were not applied at start
alerts.message: When the container started, Stella's settings and safety guards could not be fully applied. She runs, but some guards may be missing.
alerts.action: ask Claude Code to apply Stella's settings again and read the output.
alerts.cause: bin/apply-hermes-local.sh failed at container start: owner settings missing, a SOUL placeholder error, or the ~/.hermes volume unreadable.
alerts.check: run bin/apply-hermes-local.sh in the container and read its output; .supervisor/logs (container start).
alerts.related: D44; bin/container-start.sh (still sends its own text: a reboot-relevant file, not converted)

alerts.title: Stella was restarted by the recovery script
alerts.message: At {now} the Windows recovery script found part of Stella not running and started it again: {restarted}. Her last healthy check was at {last_ok}.
alerts.action: nothing, Stella is running again.
alerts.cause: Windows rebooted or slept, Docker Desktop stopped, or the container or its gateway session died.
alerts.check: the recovery log on Windows (docs/recovery.md); `hermes status` in the container.

alerts.title: Stella was restarted, but something still fails
alerts.message: At {now} the Windows recovery script found part of Stella not running and started it again: {restarted}. Her last healthy check was at {last_ok}. Still not working: {failing}.
alerts.action: run the Windows recovery script again; if it still fails, see STL-RCV-503 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: One recovery step failed (often the local model server, Ollama, or the firewall step) while the rest came back.
alerts.check: the recovery log on Windows (docs/recovery.md); `hermes status` in the container.

alerts.title: Stella's network protection is incomplete
alerts.message: The Windows recovery script restarted or repaired something, but the internet restrictions she runs under are not fully in place, even after they were applied again. Found: {parts}.
alerts.action: ask Claude Code to check and repair the network protection (see STL-RCV-504 in docs/alert-codes.md). This message is sent at most once every 6 hours for the same problem.
alerts.cause: init-firewall.sh did not build the full ruleset (the container image is older than the current script, a rule was added by hand, or a step failed), or the check could not run. The Windows recovery script probes the rules itself and names each failed check by a short token.
alerts.check: the recovery log on Windows (docs/recovery.md): the lines `firewall probe failed: <tokens>` and `firewall still failing after re-apply: <tokens>`; `bin/firewall-check.sh` as root in the container; `iptables -S` there.

parts.policy: the network is not closed by default
parts.web443: web access is not limited to the normal secure port
parts.ssh: secure remote connections are open to servers other than GitHub
parts.lan: part of the private network is open
parts.dns: name lookups are not limited to the trusted lookup server
parts.reject: the final block rule is missing
parts.ollama: the rule for the local model server is missing
parts.ipv6: the newer kind of internet address (IPv6) is not closed
parts.sets: the lists of allowed addresses are missing
parts.unchecked: the protection could not be checked at all
parts.extra: a rule lets traffic through that the firewall setup never creates (for example all outgoing traffic, or plain web on port 80)
parts._other: another problem that this message does not describe yet

alerts.title: a profile has no role, or the role table is broken
alerts.message: The role table has a gap: {problem}. Until it is fixed, that profile can create, complete, claim or delegate nothing, and cannot write to the stack's files or settings.
alerts.action: add the profile's row to the role table (roles.json), or fix the file, then ask Claude Code to re-apply the settings; see STL-CFG-303 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A new Hermes profile was created without a row in docs/hermes-local/roles.json, a row names a profile that no longer exists, or roles.json was edited into invalid JSON or an unknown value.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/roles.py check`; `bin/apply-hermes-local.sh --check` (re-applies with `bin/apply-hermes-local.sh`).

alerts.title: a data file is invalid
alerts.message: A data file that Stella reads is not valid: {problem}. What the file describes is treated as unavailable until it is fixed.
alerts.action: fix the entry the message names, then run the check again. See STL-CFG-310 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A hand edit or a change broke a data file's schema, or an entry names something that does not exist (a provider, a role, a feature).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py check` (one line per problem).

alerts.title: a name is not in the data files
alerts.message: A request named something that is not in Stella's data files: {problem}. It was refused and nothing was changed.
alerts.action: add the entry to its data file, or correct the name. See STL-CFG-311 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A typo, or an entry that was never added (a new provider, app, channel, capability or extension).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py list` and `get`; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (the requested name).

alerts.title: an owner-only action was refused: not the owner's path
alerts.message: An action on an owner-only setting, data file or command was refused because it did not come through the owner's path: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: if this was you, make the change as the owner, through the apply command; if not, look at the card or role the message names. See STL-CFG-312 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A worker or another role tried to read or change an owner-only setting, data file or state file, or to run an owner-only command, or a card branch changed owner data.
alerts.check: the event log and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.
alerts.related: F1 owner-only write path; bin/roles.py, bin/settings.py, bin/stella-apply.py, bin/merge-card.sh

alerts.title: a settings change failed and nothing was changed
alerts.message: A change to a setting or data file failed: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: fix the problem named, then try the change again. See STL-CFG-313 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The new value did not pass the schema or the cross-file rules, or the file could not be written.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`.

alerts.title: a data file or setting was changed by hand
alerts.message: A data file or setting no longer matches what was last applied: {problem}. It was changed outside the apply command.
alerts.action: review the change, then apply it properly or roll it back. See STL-CFG-314 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Someone edited the file directly instead of using the apply command.
alerts.check: the apply command's check mode shows the drift.

alerts.title: a setting value was rejected
alerts.message: A setting value was rejected: {problem}. The old value is still in use.
alerts.action: enter a value in the form the setting allows. See STL-CFG-315 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The value does not match the setting's type or validation in the settings registry.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py get settings <key>` shows the allowed form.

alerts.title: there is no backup that can be restored
alerts.message: There is no backup the apply tool can restore or trust: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: do what the message says (it names the backup folder or the file, and the repair). See STL-CFG-316 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The file was never changed through the apply command, its backups were cleaned up, or a backup folder is damaged or was not made by the apply tool.
alerts.check: the backup folder named in `.stella/data-files.json`.

alerts.title: a change needs the owner's confirmation
alerts.message: A change was not made because it needs the owner's confirmation and did not get it: {problem}.
alerts.action: run the change again from a terminal and confirm it when asked. See STL-CFG-317 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The setting is identity-critical, or no terminal was available to ask on.
alerts.check: the setting's sensitivity in `.stella/settings.json`.

alerts.title: the event log could not be written or read
alerts.message: The event log could not be written, or a line of it could not be read: {problem}. A change is never kept without its log line.
alerts.action: fix the log folder (space, permissions), then try the change again; an unreadable line is skipped by readers and can be looked at by hand. See STL-CFG-318 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The disk is full, the folder is read-only, the log file is locked, or a line in the log is not a whole event line.
alerts.check: the event log path in `.stella/data-files.json`; free space and permissions.

alerts.title: a data file is known but not readable through this tool
alerts.message: A request named a data file that Stella knows but is not readable through this tool: {problem}. It was refused and nothing was changed.
alerts.action: the file's keys are read by the apply tool; use that tool, or name a JSON data file. See STL-CFG-319 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The data file is in env format; the owner's file is never opened by this tool.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py list` shows the data files and their formats.

alerts.title: a hard-coded name is used more than its baseline allows
alerts.message: A name that must come from the data files (a provider, model, host, board, project, channel or role) is written into a script or a prompt more often than its baseline allows: {problem}. The lines after this one give each file, the name and the count.
alerts.action: move the value to the data file it belongs in and read it from there, or ask the owner to raise the baseline in hardcode-allow.json. See STL-CFG-320 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A change wrote a name into code or text instead of reading it from data, or removed a use that the baseline still counts.
alerts.check: `bin/hardcode-lint.sh --dump` (every file, name and count); `bin/hardcode-lint.sh` (the uses over the baseline).

alerts.title: a change stopped after it had started
alerts.message: A change to a setting or data file stopped after it had started: {problem}. Now on disk: {detail}.
alerts.action: run the command the message names first; it finishes or undoes the change. See STL-CFG-321 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A write failed (disk full, a folder made read-only, the event log not writable) or the run was interrupted, and putting things back failed too or was not possible after the event line.
alerts.check: `bin/stella-apply.py check <id>`; `bin/stella-apply.py history <id> --json` (the backups and their status).

alerts.title: a check or read of the data files was refused
alerts.message: A check or a read of the data files could not read everything it needed: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: fix the path or the index row the message names, then run the check again. See STL-CFG-322 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A row's file is a link, a hard link, a mount point or not a regular file, two rows name one file, or a name was given in a form the row does not take.
alerts.check: `bin/stella-apply.py check` (one line per problem; the other rows are still checked).

alerts.title: a change of a data file is unfinished
alerts.message: A change to a data file or setting was interrupted and is not finished: {problem}.
alerts.action: run the command the message names; it finishes or undoes the change. See STL-CFG-323 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: An apply or a rollback was stopped (a kill, a crash, a failed write) before its bookkeeping was done.
alerts.check: `bin/stella-apply.py history <id> --json` (the backups and their status).

alerts.title: a card was not completed: worker identity missing
alerts.message: Card {card} was not completed: the request did not come from that card's own worker run ({missing}). The card stays open.
alerts.action: nothing while its worker is still on it. If the card is stuck, complete it from the command line: see "Completing a stuck card" in SUPERVISOR.md.
alerts.cause: Someone other than the card's worker tried to complete it (the dispatcher, a background review, another card's worker), or the worker's run identity did not reach the guard.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (STL-GRD-601 lines: card, missing, profile); `hermes kanban show <card>` (assignee, runs).

alerts.title: no cards can be created: project list unreadable
alerts.message: No card can be created on board {board} right now: the list of projects bound to it could not be read, so every new card is refused.
alerts.action: ask Claude Code to check the projects list (STL-GRD-602 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: Hermes's projects.db is missing, locked or damaged, or the board has no project bound to it.
alerts.check: `hermes project list`; `hermes project show <slug>` (board, primary folder); .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (the raw error).

alerts.title: a worker could not be identified
alerts.message: Stella could not tell which card a worker run belongs to ({missing}), so card {card}'s worker cannot write in its own folder. This is a fault in Stella, not in the card or the worker.
alerts.action: nothing on the card. Ask Claude Code to check worker identity (STL-GRD-603 in docs/alert-codes.md); the card's escalation thread opens when its worker stops and asks.
alerts.cause: A builder guard needed the card's worktree and could not prove the run from the board and the process tree while the profile had a running card: the board was unreadable, the run's worker binding was missing, or the hook was not below the bound worker process.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (`grep STL-GRD-603`: card, profile and the proof that failed); `hermes kanban show <card> --json` (worker_bound and claimed events of the open run).

alerts.title: a tool call was refused by the rules of its role
alerts.message: A tool call was refused by the rules of the role that made it: {problem}. Nothing was run or changed.
alerts.action: nothing when the role works as designed. If a role needs this tool or command, the owner changes its row in docs/hermes-local/roles.json. See STL-GRD-604 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A guard of a role refused a call the role does not allow: a coordinator write, a builder's write outside its card worktree or its git push to main, a reviewer's write, a tool the role names no matcher for, a read of a secret path.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (`grep STL-GRD-604`: the role, the card where there is one, and what was refused).
alerts.related: K8, B.1 (F1 W4 round 5); the hooks under docs/hermes-local/hooks/, bin/roles.py hook_refusal

alerts.title: a card was blocked without an escalation
alerts.message: Card {card} ("{title}") was blocked ({by}) and no escalation was opened for it, so it is being posted in #escalations now. Reason: {reason}.
alerts.action: answer in the card's #escalations thread, or archive the card if it is no longer needed.
alerts.cause: Hermes blocked the card without a block event (for example the dispatcher gave up after its retry limit), so the normal escalation hook never ran.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (SILENT_BLOCK for the card); `hermes kanban show <card>` (events).

alerts.title: a worker's model calls keep failing
alerts.message: Card {card}'s worker has had {count} failed model calls in the last {minutes} minutes and has done no work in that time: {parts}. The card stays open while this lasts.
alerts.action: fix what the cause names (start the model server, or load the worker's model and unload others), then wait for the next check; see STL-MDL-701 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The worker's session logged model-call errors (connection errors, stalled streams) and no completed tool call within the window.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (`grep STL-MDL-701`: the model server address and the loaded models); the worker profile's logs/agent.log for the session.
alerts.resolved_title: a worker's model calls work again
alerts.resolved_message: Card {card}'s worker gets model answers again, or the card stopped running. The problem lasted from {since} to {now}.

parts.unreachable: the model server its profile uses does not answer
parts.not_loaded: no model is loaded on that server
parts.other_loaded: another model is loaded on that server instead of the worker's own, likely filling the GPU
parts.loaded: the server answers and the worker's model is loaded, so the calls fail for another reason
parts.unknown: the check could not tell why
parts._other: the check could not tell why

alerts.title: the check for failing model calls cannot run
alerts.message: The check that spots workers whose model calls keep failing could not run {count} times in a row. Until it runs again, a worker stuck on failing model calls is not reported.
alerts.action: see why in .supervisor/logs/watchdog.log ("model watch could not check") and run python3 bin/model_watch.py by hand; usually the board cannot be read or the model_watch settings are invalid (python3 bin/watchdog_settings.py --check); see STL-MDL-702 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: bin/model_watch.py exited non-zero or printed something that is not a JSON list, on several watchdog runs in a row (WATCHDOG_MODEL_WATCH_FAILS_N, default 2).
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/watchdog.log; python3 bin/model_watch.py; python3 bin/watchdog_settings.py --check.
alerts.resolved_title: the check for failing model calls runs again
alerts.resolved_message: The check for failing model calls runs again. It could not run from {since} to {now}.

alerts.title: something needs a look
alerts.message: A part of Stella reported a problem, but its description is missing from the alert list ({requested}). {summary}
alerts.action: see STL-GEN-000 in docs/alert-codes.md, and ask Claude Code to add the missing description.
alerts.cause: A script asked for an alert code that is not in docs/hermes-local/alert-catalog.json, or the alert could not be rendered (catalog unreadable, python3 missing).
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (the requested code and the raw details).
